USMLE-style practice · Orthopedics

monteggia — clinical decision 2

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 40-year-old patient has a displaced ulnar shaft fracture with radial head dislocation after a motorcycle crash. During operative planning, the surgeon identifies the bony correction that usually permits the radial head to reduce. Which correction is most important?

  1. Fix the distal radius despite its normal alignment
  2. Fuse the distal radioulnar joint immediately
  3. Restore ulnar length and anatomical alignment
  4. Shorten the ulna to reduce soft-tissue tension
  5. Remove the intact radial head routinely
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Restore ulnar length and anatomical alignment

The ulna provides the structural relationship needed for reduction and stability of the radial head.

Understanding the options

Restore ulnar length and anatomical alignment
The ulna provides the structural relationship needed for reduction and stability of the radial head.
Shorten the ulna to reduce soft-tissue tension
Ulnar shortening may compromise the radiocapitellar relationship.
Remove the intact radial head routinely
Routine excision is not the primary treatment for this fracture-dislocation.
Fix the distal radius despite its normal alignment
The primary shaft injury in this case involves the ulna.
Fuse the distal radioulnar joint immediately
Distal fusion does not correct the proximal fracture-dislocation.
